newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude called higher following gasoline, IPE.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude called higher following gasoline, IPE.

text.p: NYMEX crude was called five to 10 cents higher a barrel Friday following strength of Brent futures on London's IPE amid continued buying interest in gasoline.
"We are following London, and there is also follow-through buying of gasoline on the talk of refinery problems," said a New York dealer.
Gasoline was called 0.25 cent a gallon higher while heating oil was called steady to 0.25 cent a gallon up.
Gasoline has been strong all week following news of declining gasoline stocks and unconfirmed talk of refinery problems in the U.S. Gulf.
There also has been little evidence of refinery buying in the gasoline cash markets to suggest operational problems.

"I think we have found a bottom in gasoline around the 60.00 cent area after lagging heating oil in the past weeks. Also, the gasoline cracks are recovering well which is a good sign," said a New York gasoline dealer.
Meanwhile, June Brent was up 12 cents at $18.81 a barrel on active volume on the IPE.
June crude here settled 72 cents higher Thursday at $20.34 a barrel, the first close above $20.00 since April 30, leaving it poised to test key resistance between $20.50 and $20.60.
Prompt crude has tested and failed at that resistance area four times since April 21.
June gasoline ended 1.58 cents higher a gallon at 62.50 cents while June heating oil finished 1.30 cents a gallon at 54.38 cents.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
